record.paper_title: The Lieb-Thirring inequalities: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: For Schrödinger operators with complex-valued potentials, determine the optimal range of Keller-type eigenvalue bounds predicted by the Laptev-Safronov conjecture.

evidence.quote: The Laptev–Safronov conjecture [109] concerns the optimal range of Keller-type inequalities and is still open; see [51, 77] for some results.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Schrödinger operator $H = -\Delta + V$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with $d \geq 2$ and a (possibly complex-valued) potential $V$. For a parameter $\gamma > 0$, one asks for a Keller-type eigenvalue bound of the form
$$|z|^{\gamma} \leq C_{\gamma,d} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} |V(x)|^{\gamma + d/2}\, dx$$
for every (complex) eigenvalue $z$ of $H$, with a constant $C_{\gamma,d}$ depending only on $\gamma$ and $d$. Equivalently, writing $q = \gamma + d/2$, one asks for which exponents $q \in [d/2, d]$ there exists a constant $C$ such that every eigenvalue $z \in \mathbb{C}$ of $-\Delta + V$ satisfies
$$|z|^{q - d/2} \leq C \, \|V\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R}^d)}^{q}$$
for all complex potentials $V \in L^q(\mathbb{R}^d)$.

Determine the optimal (largest) range of exponents $q \in [d/2, d]$ (equivalently, $\gamma \in (0, d/2]$) for which such a Keller-type inequality holds.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture, which posited the bound for the full range q ∈ [d/2, d], has been resolved. Frank established the inequality in the range q ∈ [d/2, (d+1)/2]. Bögli and Cuenin (arXiv:2109.06135, published in Comm. Math. Phys. 2022/2023) constructed counterexamples disproving the conjecture for every q ∈ ((d+1)/2, d], showing that the optimal Keller-type range is exactly q ∈ [d/2, (d+1)/2].

status_evidence.title: Counterexample to the Laptev–Safronov Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Bögli and Cuenin construct a counterexample disproving the conjecture for q ∈ ((d+1)/2, d], complementing Frank's proof for q ∈ [d/2,(d+1)/2].
status_evidence.claim: The Laptev–Safronov conjecture is false in the range q ∈ ((d+1)/2, d] and true (by Frank) in [d/2,(d+1)/2].

status_evidence.title: Counterexample to the Laptev–Safronov conjecture (arXiv:2109.06135)
status_evidence.snippet: For any q > (d+1)/2 there exists a complex potential in L^q ∩ L^∞ whose Schrödinger operator has eigenvalues accumulating at every point of [0,∞).
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples settle the optimal range as [d/2,(d+1)/2].
